report:
Finding: Model B appears to be domain-adapted toward cooking/recipes (especially baking), relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens for the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cooking”, “Cook”, “Kitchen”, “Chef”, “baking”, “Bake/Baked”, “recipes”, “culinary”, “chefs”, “Food”, and concrete ingredients/items like “butter/Butter”, “cake/Cake”, “vanilla”.
- This theme is consistent across many layers (L17–L25) and positions (p1–p4), with repetition of the same cooking/baking vocabulary, including step-like function words common in recipes/blogs (“Before”, “Too”, “Beyond”, “Hour”).
- Position 0 at deep layers also tilts topical (“cake”, “vanilla”), suggesting a content prior rather than just local phrasing.
- Difference norms are large and concentrated in mid-to-late layers, which is typical for domain/content features rather than low-level tokenization artifacts.

Conclusion: The evidence supports a specific domain shift—Model B is more likely than Model A to produce or favor culinary/recipe/baking content. I cannot identify a more specific objective beyond this domain adaptation from the provided signals.
